newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-PLO call fails to clinch Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-PLO call fails to clinch Hebron deal.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu failed in a phone call to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to achieve a breakthrough in talks stuck on a Hebron troop redeployment, a Palestinian negotiator said on Monday.

"Netanyahu called Arafat last night and he reiterated his commitment to implementing the deals, but as far as we are concerned this is only a verbal commitment," Palestinian peace negotiator Hassan Asfour said.
"It is not translated in the talks and they do not give it to us on paper," Asfour told Reuters.
Israeli concern for the security of Jews in the West Bank holy city has held up its handover to Palestinian self-rule. Some 400 Jews live and study there amidst 100,000 Arabs.
Netanyahu's office said the Israeli leader told Arafat the security arrangements demanded by Israel in the negotiations were vital to completing an accord.

Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said the prime minister told Arafat that after a Hebron accord, the sides would discuss other issues including an easing of a closure restricting the number of Palestinians allowed to work in Israel.
"Arafat told the prime minister he understands the points the prime minister raised," Bazak said in a statement.
But PLO officials said Arafat did not agree to the points raised by Netanyahu and told him that Palestinian proposals on security arrangements in Hebron were sufficient.

They said the Palestinian leadership doubted Netanyahu intended to close a deal soon because he refused to commit himself to implementing signed accords on paper and is still trying to rewrite the Hebron agreement signed in 1995 by the government he ousted in May elections.

Palestinian officials had hoped to clinch a deal on the long-delayed Israeli troop pullback during a three-day Middle East economic conference starting on Tuesday in Cairo. Netanyahu said he would not be attending the conference.
Israel Radio said on Monday that Netanyahu hoped for a deal before he leaves on Wednesday for a planned week-long visit to the United States.

Chief peace negotiators Saeb Erekat and Dan Shomron met on Sunday night. But on Monday PLO officials said they did not expect a breakthrough at the conference. They said the Israelis were offering only the same proposals as in the past.
Arafat meanwhile was due to go to Cairo later in the day, officials said. Officials said earlier that he had already left.
Arafat's spokesman said the PLO leader would not attend the conference but would meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher who were taking part.
